subject: Staged billing cadence & VAT withholding for EU pilot - Skyport Analytics
messages:
From: Amir Khan <amir@skyport.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Fischer <lena.fischer@skyport.io>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Billing cadence for EU pilot & VAT withholding request

Hi Sean —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re excited to kick off the EU pilot (Skyport Analytics / Redwood). A couple of billing items finance needs clarified before we sign:

- Our EU procurement team needs the ability to withhold VAT at source on invoices for the pilot entity in Frankfurt. Can Redwood support invoices that explicitly show VAT withheld and a net payable line?
- Given this is a short pilot (2 months), we’d like Net45 terms rather than Net30, and a provisional credit cap to avoid up-front prepayment. Can you propose a provisional cap?
- If possible, could you share an invoice template and an SOW we can push to our legal/finance for review?

Appreciate a quick run-through — our finance/operations folks are cc’d.

—Amir
Amir Khan
Head of Platform Ops, Skyport Analytics
amir@skyport.io

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Amir Khan <amir@skyport.io>
Cc: Lena Fischer <lena.fischer@skyport.io>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing cadence for EU pilot & VAT withholding request

Hi Amir —

Thanks — excited to get Skyport running. Quick read on each ask and a proposal we think balances cashflow + compliance:

1) VAT withholding: yes, we can support invoices that include a VAT-withheld line and show gross VAT and net payable. That will be conditional on receipt of a valid EU VAT registration certificate for your paying entity. Please attach the certificate (PDF).

2) Payment terms & credit cap: for a short pilot we typically offer either Net30 with a lower provisional cap or Net45 with a slightly higher provisional cap. Our proposed default:
   - Staged invoicing cadence: monthly usage invoices (net of any withholding) + a milestone invoice for onboarding professional services on day 30.
   - Provisional credit cap: $50,000 for the first 30 days; automatic review and potential expansion to $100,000 if usage tracks to forecast and we have VAT evidence.
   - If Skyport needs Net45 specifically, finance will require the VAT cert up front (see #1) and we’ll add a 60-day review clause.

3) Early-pay: we can offer a small cash discount for early payment (sample: 1–2% within 10 days). Our finance team will confirm the final percentage.

I’ve attached an invoice template that shows the withholding line and an updated SOW (draft) for the EU pilot — see attachments: RI_invoice_template_EU.pdf and SOW draft (SOW_Skyport_EU_Pilot_v1.0). I’ll loop in Evelyn and Naomi on the credit/ops approval.

Next steps: Amir, can you send the VAT registration PDF and confirm whether Skyport prefers Net45 or Net30 for the pilot? If you prefer Net45, we’ll flag it for provisional cap review with finance. Also let us know if you want the SOW adjusted (billing milestones, acceptance criteria).

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Account Executive — Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com

From: Amir Khan <amir@skyport.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Fischer <lena.fischer@skyport.io>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing cadence for EU pilot & VAT withholding request

Sean —

Thanks for the fast response. Attached is the VAT cert for the Skyport GmbH entity in Frankfurt (SKY_VAT_CERT_2026.pdf).

We’d like to proceed with Net45 for the pilot given internal cashflow windows. The provisional cap of $50k is a bit low for our forecasted throughput — can you do $80k provisional for the first 30 days, with a 60-day review? If finance needs a counter-proposal we can discuss.

Also: Skyport is open to an early-pay discount; 2%/10 would work on our side if Redwood can confirm.

I’ve attached the VAT cert and will push the SOW to our legal once we have the invoice template.

Best,
—Amir
Amir Khan
amir@skyport.io

Attachment: SKY_VAT_CERT_2026.pdf
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Amir Khan <amir@skyport.io>
Cc: Lena Fischer <lena.fischer@skyport.io>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing cadence for EU pilot & VAT withholding request

Hi team — quick update from finance and legal after reviewing Amir’s VAT cert and Sean’s proposal.

Summary of agreed provisional terms (for pilot signature):
- Credit cap: Redwood will provisionally approve $75,000 for the first 60 days (compromise between $50k and $80k). Cap will be reevaluated at day 60 and may be increased with normal underwriting (usage trends + payment history).
- Payment terms: Net45 for Skyport GmbH for the duration of the 60-day provisional window, contingent on receipt of the VAT cert (received).
- VAT withholding: Accepted. Invoices will include: gross amount, VAT amount, VAT withheld (if applicable), and net payable. Finance needs the withholding line formatted exactly as in the attached invoice template (RI_invoice_template_EU.pdf) to allow Skyport to remit on their side.
- Early-pay: Redwood can offer 1.5% if paid within 10 days (1.5%/10). Please confirm if Skyport prefers 1.5% or 2%.
- SOW & signature: I’ve attached an updated SOW with the provisional cap and Net45 terms baked in (SOW_Skyport_EU_Pilot_v1.1.pdf). DocuSign link is below for execution.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/s/SKYPORT_SOW_2026

Amir/Lena — if that reads clean, please confirm and we’ll route the DocuSign for signature and issue the first invoice at the agreed cadence.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Finance — Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com

Attachments: RI_invoice_template_EU.pdf, SOW_Skyport_EU_Pilot_v1.1.pdf
